feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/operations leadership. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within one organization strongly signal trust, growth, and leadership.  
- Good scope and relevance: combines strategy, web/CMS, analytics, content, and multimedia in a way that fits modern digital leadership roles.  
- Generally strong writing: concise, professional, and easy to follow, with no major spelling errors or obvious typos.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than outcomes. Include measurable impact where possible (growth %, engagement lifts, efficiency gains, cost savings, adoption rates).  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily. Consolidating would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12+ years of experience” instead of “more than 12 years experience”; standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia”); and keep punctuation/hyphenation consistent (e.g., “organization-wide,” “member-facing,” date abbreviations like “Sept.” vs “Mar.”).
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns well with the CV’s senior digital leadership focus. It would be sharper with a more distinctive opening, tighter phrasing, and clearer emphasis on recent strengths in platform modernization, governance, and mission-driven communications.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years’ experience” for cleaner style and correct grammar.
- Lead with current market positioning: “Digital communications and strategy leader” rather than “professional.”
- Add outcomes-oriented language tied to recent roles, e.g., enterprise web platforms, editorial systems, analytics, and cross-functional governance.
- Tighten the final sentence to avoid generic phrasing and improve flow.

Possible rewrite:
Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years’ experience leading web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel communications, platform modernization, editorial workflows, and the systems that enable coordinated, large-scale publishing. Strong in advocacy messaging, stakeholder alignment, and translating technical or policy issues into clear, accessible content.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the language and emphasizing higher-value, current capabilities will make it sharper and more distinctive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic phrases with more senior, specific terms: “Digital transformation” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation,” “Editorial systems & governance” instead of “Editorial workflow design.”
- Reduce overlap and group related items for clarity. Suggested version: Digital transformation • Multi-channel communications leadership • Web platform & CMS administration • Editorial systems & governance • Analytics, reporting & optimization • Workflow architecture & automation • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia & live event production
- Standardize style: use “communications” instead of “communication” for consistency with the rest of the CV.
- Consider dropping “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination,” which reads more like a soft skill than a core competency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with Topline Skills; if both sections remain, make Core Competencies shorter and more strategic.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” duplicates Soft Skills almost exactly.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and project footer. Tighten it around 3–5 high-impact contributions and add outcomes, scale, or named initiatives where possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper lead: “Embedded consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform strategy, Drupal campaign delivery, and communications operations modernization.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into outcome-oriented points, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign microsites and modular storytelling components, including downloadable member toolkits, to speed campaign launches and improve reuse across teams.
- Standardized cross-channel workflows, governance, and analytics for web, email, social, and multimedia communications.
- Led AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, publishing teams, turnaround reduction, engagement lift, search success, or traffic.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also overlap with the summary and NACo role.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes, team/enterprise scope, and avoid repeating channel-management details covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, video production, and multi-channel communications strategy.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes:
- “Led redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing internal capacity for advocacy programming, event production, and recurring video content.”
- “Implemented enterprise analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, strengthening reporting and decision-making.”
- “Established digital governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning systems to improve consistency and operational efficiency.”
- If possible, add 1–2 measurable results on email/social growth, reporting speed, cost savings, or production volume.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on transformation and leadership-level impact.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; use this item for enterprise-scale achievements.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Make it more specific to what changed under your ownership at this level, with sharper action verbs and any available volume/growth metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize scope and level: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy publishing across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more impact-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one stronger systems bullet: “Built more consistent editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content delivery.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening line.
- “weekly advocacy video update” also overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer entry and Recent Projects.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline skills item overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent experience. It should be tightened to emphasize leadership scope and distinctive strengths rather than restating broad digital/comms terms.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-value language tied to current senior roles.
- Use parallel noun phrases and remove overlap with “Core Competencies.”
- Consider:  
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation  
- Editorial governance & content operations  
- Cross-channel communications leadership  
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications  
- Audience strategy, messaging & content planning
- If space allows, swap “content planning” for “stakeholder-aligned communications strategy” if targeting more senior leadership roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications leadership” substantially duplicate the header and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; keep it only if this section needs sector positioning.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should be tighter, more strategic, and weighted toward the platforms and capabilities most evident in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability-led wording, e.g.: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal and CMS modernization first; they are most supported by recent experience. Consider dropping or de-emphasizing WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages unless central to target roles.
- Replace “Airtable systems” with “Airtable-based content systems” or “Airtable workflow systems” for clearer business value.
- Keep this section concise; let the Technical + IT section carry the full platform inventory.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search experiences” duplicates Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it here only if phrased more technically.
- Most listed tools repeat the “Technical + IT” section almost verbatim.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a software inventory rather than a senior capability statement. It also overlaps heavily with “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT, so this section should emphasize strategic application over tool repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to outcome-oriented leadership language, e.g.:
- Analytics strategy and KPI design
- Executive and leadership reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Power BI and Looker Studio
- User behavior insights, SEO and performance optimization
- Consider replacing “Microsoft Clarity” with “behavior analytics” if you want this section to feel more senior and less tool-specific.
- Tighten “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO and digital performance optimization.”
- Order by value: strategy/reporting first, platforms second, optimization last.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- If kept here, use this section for strategic framing and leave the full tool list to Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- Video production and editing

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid skill cluster, but it’s generic and overlaps with both Core Competencies and Technical + IT. Tighten it to emphasize higher-level production capability and recent studio/event leadership rather than listing basic tasks.

- Replace with more outcome-oriented, senior phrasing:

- “Livestreaming” and “Hybrid and virtual event production” substantially overlap; combine them.
- This section repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” from Core Competencies and tool details from Technical + IT.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too generic for a senior candidate. It also overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” so it should emphasize platform depth and recency rather than repeat a simple tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to show level of use: “Drupal (enterprise modernization, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages”
- Put the strongest, most recent platform first and consider trimming weaker/older tools if space is tight.
- If accurate, add scope in parentheses for the lead platform, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)” to connect skills to impact.
- Consider renaming the heading to “CMS & Web Platforms” for slightly stronger phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages.
- GitHub Pages may feel lightweight versus the rest; remove it unless it supports a recent project or portfolio use.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, AI search, and workflow work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Rewrite as: **HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery, API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions**
- If accurate, add specificity instead of more tools: **JavaScript-based front-end enhancements, third-party/API integrations, tag deployment via GTM, edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers, CI/CD support with GitHub Actions**
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless matching ATS language elsewhere; plain **HTML, CSS** is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**.
- If space is tight, keep the fuller version in one place only and use this section for tools not named elsewhere.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems leadership. Since “workflow automation” already appears in Core Competencies and Topline Skills, this item should be tighter and more clearly framed around systems you actually build or manage.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by strategic relevance: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light functional grouping for clarity: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Collaboration:** Slack, Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, replace one or two generic tools with higher-signal phrasing: **Airtable workflow systems • Power Automate flows • Zapier integrations**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” is already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating that exact phrase elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams/Basecamp are lower-impact than Airtable/Power Automate/Zapier/Jira, so keep them secondary.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Given the strong email leadership already shown in recent NACo roles, this item should be tighter and framed to signal enterprise-scale campaign operations.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Replace with: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If space allows, add light functional context: **enterprise email automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was minimal or older, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with work-experience bullets about leading email newsletters reaching tens of thousands; avoid repeating outcomes here
- “Multi-channel communications” and email leadership already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills, so keep this item platform-specific rather than descriptive

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale/results you can add.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and hands-on production: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team, improving execution across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 concrete outcomes if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, video cadence, audience growth, or process improvements.
- Tighten the second sentence: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates, and provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”
- If true, specify tools/platforms or operational impact: CMS migration support, faster publishing, more consistent cross-channel delivery, reduced vendor reliance.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” repeats the 2018–2022 role; frame this version as launching or piloting the format.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with later governance/operations bullets; keep this entry more executional.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially launching the first podcast. It should be tightened and framed around ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and initiative: “Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting NACo program and policy priorities.”
- Make the digital work more specific and active: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications, including planning and developing supporting materials.”
- Highlight the standout achievement with clearer ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting, and production.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; keep this item focused on research/program support plus the podcast launch.
- Avoid broad claims about digital leadership here, since stronger evidence appears in 2015–2024 roles.
